question_type: Difference of calendar-year sums of monthly national-defense expenditures (1953 vs 1940), with the 1940 sum restated in 1953 dollars using external CPI-U values

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: For 1940, Opus used the 1941_01/1941_02 table 'Budget Expenditures Classified as General, by Major Functions', printed at the time, and its narrower 'National defense' function column. Its search never found Table 6B 'Detail of Expenditures by Months and Years' in the Feb 1952 and Feb 1953 bulletins. That table prints the 1940 months under the same label as the 1953 series, 'National defense and related activities - Total'. Two gaps caused the miss. Step 4 grepped only 1941_0[1-3] and 1954_0[1-3]. scan_tables.py only matched tables with 'defense' in the header row and 'YYYY - Month' row labels, but Table 6B is a year-by-month horizontal grid whose series label sits in a spanning row.
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: The prompt arm applied its verified lesson L-defense-table6b-calendar-months, learned from sibling question ordinal 55 (UID0004). The lesson names Table 6B as the only calendar-year-by-month defense table. The arm grep-verified the 1940 row in 1953_02 ([8]) and the 1953 monthly cells ([10]), summed the monthly cells rather than using the printed row total, and converted 1940 to 1953 dollars ([3]-[4], [11]).
opus_divergence.evidence: Opus: worklog.md:15-27 (steps 3-8); scan_tables.py:19 (header-only 'defense' match); solution.json decisions[0] 'Which 1940 vintage'; review.md check 3 ('grepped 1942-1959 issues for 1940 monthly rows and found no defense series'). Prompt AGENTS.md:265-272 and 1413-1433 (lesson text, verified_by postmortem:055). GLM prompt digest: [1], [8], [10], [11].

reviewer_flag: Verdict confirmed. The residual risks it listed (mixed-vintage 1940, the published calendar-year total, a 1982-84 base) did not include the Table 6B series or the CPI values. The reviewer's own grep also missed Table 6B.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Principled for the source table: the arm followed a verified lesson from another question that encodes the key's source table and the convention of summing the monthly cells. Unclear for the CPI values, which it recalled from memory, as Opus did.
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: No. cards found Table 6B on its own ([29]-[31]). It then 'repaired' one 1940 monthly cell, assuming an OCR error, so that the months summed to the printed row total ([72]-[82]). It used the same CPI pair as prompt and landed within_0.1pct, but was graded wrong. none ran 2848 s and 259 requests through several context compactions. It took a single 1940 cell from an annual table as the 'monthly sum', used the published 1953 calendar-year total, and used a different 1940 CPI value (5-25pct). Neither arm used Opus's 1941-bulletin 'National defense' series.
lesson_for_harness: (1) For multi-year sums of a named series, prefer one table that prints both endpoints under the question's series label (label consistency) over a table printed at the time that uses a narrower classification. Search must cover every table layout, including horizontal month grids and series labels in spanning rows, not only header-row matches. (2) Cross-question memory (STATE) decided this item: the prompt arm's only advantage was a verified lesson from another question on the same series. (3) Grading is effectively exact at hundredths: cards was off by about 0.005% and scored 0. So small external-knowledge differences matter, and 'repairing' printed monthly cells to match a printed total is harmful when the question says to use the monthly values.
notes: Opus also diverged a second time, on EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE. Its recalled 1953 annual CPI-U was one tenth of an index point lower than the value both adapted GLM arms recalled. cards used the same CPI as prompt, and its 1940 sum was only one unit different, yet it was graded wrong. The grading tolerance is therefore much tighter than the effect of that CPI difference (about 0.05%), so Opus would most likely have failed on the CPI value alone even with Table 6B. This is an inference from the grades, not checked against the Minneapolis Fed table (no web). Opus, prompt and cards agreed on the 1953 monthly cells and summed the months; none used the printed calendar-year total for 1953.
